```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(stream)
set.seed(1000)
```

`DSD_MG()` combines Moving Generator Clusters (`MGC`s) into an evolving data
stream. Each component specifies a cluster's location, shape, size, and density
over time. This guide expands on the generator introduced in the original
`stream_vignette.Rnw`, using examples from the `DSD_MG` and `MGC` help pages.

## Combine clusters and noise

Start with a Gaussian cluster, a uniform rectangular cluster, and uniform
background noise. All components must have the stream's dimensionality.
`parameter` gives standard deviations for `Shape_Gaussian` and side lengths for
`Shape_Block`.

```{r static-stream}
stream <- DSD_MG(dimension = 2,
  MGC_Static(density = 45, center = c(1, 0), parameter = 0.1),
  MGC_Static(density = 45, center = c(2, 0), parameter = c(0.4, 0.6),
    shape = Shape_Block),
  MGC_Noise(density = 10, range = rbind(c(0, 3), c(-1, 1))),
  labels = c(1, 2, NA)
)
stream
get_points(stream, n = 5)
plot(stream, n = 500, xlim = c(0, 3), ylim = c(-1, 1))
```

`density` controls both the relative chance of choosing a component and the
number of points generated per unit of generator time. Here the total density
is 100, so approximately 100 points advance the generator by one time unit.
Noise has label `NA` in the `.class` column. Supply the same label to multiple
components when they should represent one ground-truth cluster.

## Define movement with keyframes

`MGC_Linear()` interpolates the center, density, and shape parameters between
keyframes. The next example starts with one cluster. At time 50, a second
component appears at the same location, then moves in another direction.

```{r splitting-stream}
c1 <- MGC_Linear(dimension = 2, keyframelist = list(
  keyframe(time = 1, density = 20, center = c(0, 0), parameter = 5),
  keyframe(time = 50, density = 20, center = c(50, 50), parameter = 5),
  keyframe(time = 100, density = 20, center = c(50, 100), parameter = 5)
))
c2 <- MGC_Linear(dimension = 2, keyframelist = list(
  keyframe(time = 50, density = 20, center = c(50, 50), parameter = 5),
  keyframe(time = 100, density = 20, center = c(100, 50), parameter = 5)
))
stream <- DSD_MG(dimension = 2, c1, c2)
get_keyframes(c1)
```

A linear component produces no points before its first keyframe. After its last
keyframe it keeps its final attributes. A keyframe with `reset = TRUE` can make
the trajectory repeat, as in `DSD_Benchmark(1)`.

Generator time is different from the count of requested points. The second
component starts after about 980 points: 49 time units at density 20. Once it
appears, the total density becomes 40. Plot three short sections around this
change and near the end of the movement:

```{r splitting-snapshots, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.5}
local({
  old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
  on.exit(par(old_par))
  plot(stream, n = 200, xlim = c(-15, 115), ylim = c(-15, 115),
    main = "One cluster")
  invisible(get_points(stream, n = 780))
  plot(stream, n = 200, xlim = c(-15, 115), ylim = c(-15, 115),
    main = "Second cluster appears")
  invisible(get_points(stream, n = 1400))
  plot(stream, n = 200, xlim = c(-15, 115), ylim = c(-15, 115),
    main = "Separate paths")
})
```

## Add and remove components

Generators can be modified after construction. `get_clusters()` returns the
component list; `remove_cluster()` takes an index in that list.

```{r modify-stream}
noise <- MGC_Noise(density = 2, range = rbind(c(-15, 115), c(-15, 115)))
add_cluster(stream, noise, label = NA)
length(get_clusters(stream))
plot(stream, n = 500, xlim = c(-15, 115), ylim = c(-15, 115))
remove_cluster(stream, i = 3)
length(get_clusters(stream))
```

Use `add_keyframe()` and `remove_keyframe()` to edit a linear component's
trajectory. Stream and component objects contain mutable state: updating a
component can also affect a stream that contains it.

## Specify movement as a function of time

`MGC_Function()` accepts functions of generator time for density, center, and
shape parameters. Here a Gaussian cluster travels around a circle while a
static cluster remains at the center.

```{r functional-stream}
orbit <- MGC_Function(
  density = function(t) 20,
  center = function(t) c(0.5 + 0.35 * cos(t / 10),
    0.5 + 0.35 * sin(t / 10)),
  parameter = function(t) 0.03
)
stream <- DSD_MG(dimension = 2, orbit,
  MGC_Static(density = 5, center = c(0.5, 0.5), parameter = 0.03))
```

The GIF below shows the functional generator in batches of 50 points, making
the orbiting cluster's movement visible. It loops automatically at ten frames
per second and is embedded directly in the HTML.

Knitr creates the GIF using the `gifski` R package.
Install `gifski` before rendering to include the animation. The animation chunk
is skipped when `gifski` is unavailable or the output is not HTML.

```{r generator-animation, eval=knitr::is_html_output() && requireNamespace("gifski", quietly=TRUE), fig.show='animate', animation.hook='gifski', interval=0.1, aniopts='loop', dev='png', fig.width=6.4, fig.height=4.8, dpi=100, fig.retina=1, fig.alt='A moving Gaussian cluster orbiting a static cluster'}
local({
  set.seed(1000)
  reset_stream(stream)
  for (i in seq_len(30)) {
    plot(stream, n = 50, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1),
      main = paste("Moving Generator after", i * 50, "points"))
  }
})
```

For interactive exploration, the following example uses the `animation` package
and is not run during vignette builds.

```{r animation, eval=FALSE}
reset_stream(stream)
animate_data(stream, n = 1500, horizon = 100,
  xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1))
animation::ani.replay()
```
